analysis.summary: AnyTrack is the only one publishing new how-to pages on fixing tracking. Rivals mostly refresh old pages or push webinars and AI content, and two were silent.

points.text: AnyTrack published 4 new how-to pages on tracking gaps, CRM conversions and affiliate scaling, aimed at buyers fixing real problems.
RedTrack updated 5 older pages and launched 45 pages on 2026-10-29, which looks like a bulk launch or site-wide change, not new articles.
Triple Whale and RedTrack both lean on AI-for-ecommerce lists, which pulls readers away from tracking toward general ecommerce topics.

shared.title: Webinars as content
shared.text: RedTrack and Voluum both feature webinar pages on ad tracking and Q4 themes. It's event-led learning content, so AnyTrack could compete with written guides that last longer.

shared.title: AI and ecommerce topics
shared.text: Triple Whale and RedTrack both updated lists of AI tools or agents for ecommerce. This is broad, top-of-funnel content, far from tracking setup questions.

shared.title: Refresh over new pages
shared.text: RedTrack, Voluum and Triple Whale mostly updated old pages (5, 2 and 2) rather than publishing new ones. AnyTrack is the one adding fresh pages.

gaps.title: Tracking fix troubleshooting
gaps.text: No rival published guides on data mismatches between ad platforms and stores. AnyTrack's Meta-vs-Shopify page could grow into a series for Google, TikTok and others.

gaps.title: CRM to ad platform guides
gaps.text: No rival has pages on sending CRM or offline events back to ad platforms. AnyTrack can own this with one guide per CRM.

gaps.title: Comparison and buying pages
gaps.text: Rivals published almost no comparison or buying content on tracking tools. AnyTrack could write honest head-to-head and migration guides for people evaluating tools.
